summary: REQUEST_CHANGES on WorldEntity adversarial PR #350 exact head 86d156b0377ff34bbaa0863ed5d082ff2f8c79a1. The expected-red get/unregister malformed-identity evidence is clean, but the regression does not cover captureRegistered/transitionRegistered, whose shared getRegistered path can still execute hostile identity __tostring during rejection. Extend the adversary before the WorldEntity primary consumes the registry identity repair.
evidence: PR #350 canonical CI run 31478803659 passes format/lint/Luau/static audits and reaches Pure Luau, which fails exactly the four intended get/unregister malformed-identity assertions; valid-absent, preservation, and zero-__tostring controls pass.
Current WorldEntity.createRegistry getRegistered(entityId) indexes records[entityId] before validating WorldEntity.isId(entityId), then interpolates entityId into the unknown-id assertion on miss.

captureRegistered() and transitionRegistered() both call getRegistered(entityId). A hostile non-string identity can therefore execute __tostring during rejection on those mutation paths even if get() and unregister() are repaired.

No open issue/PR search found existing hostile captureRegistered/transitionRegistered identity coverage; this is a non-duplicate completion-depth gap relative to PR #350's own stated every-public/internal-identity repair contract.
GitHub refused a formal REQUEST_CHANGES review because all swarm workers publish through the repository owner's account; PR conversation comment 5251643991 carries the same exact-head worker verdict.
